title: Resolve the canonical Person once per request and batch getPerson reads
description:
`DurableAccountsService.person()` runs the full identity lookup (alias, Google record, session pointer list, each committed login record, alias and person file). `allowed()` calls it, `setMembership` calls `allowed()` and `directory.get()` on every retry attempt, and `list()` and the directory handler call it again. One request can run the lookup several times. `getPerson()` reads session pointers one at a time until one commits.

Scope:
- Resolve the Person once per request and reuse it inside the same `Context`; never cache across requests and never cache account documents or memberships.
- Batch `getPerson()` pointer reads four at a time with the same per-lookup memo `find()` uses, stopping at the first committed login.
- Move the target-person existence check out of the `setMembership` retry loop; only the account document is re-read on a CAS conflict, with the actor permission re-check kept.

Acceptance: read-counting tests prove one identity resolution per request, bounded concurrency in `getPerson`, and no repeated target lookup under a CAS conflict. All native suites pass.
